Standard Library > ws_client: WebSocket Client

ws_client.sai: WebSocket Client

An RFC 6455 WebSocket client in pure Zig (source src/runtime/sa_ws_client.zig, in the sci repository's cross-platform branch). A connection is an opaque u64 handle (0 = invalid), and connect() completes the transport layer + the HTTP Upgrade handshake in one go: ws:// goes over a direct TCP connection, and wss:// directly reuses sa_tls_client for TLS (there is no second TLS implementation, and the verification policy is exactly the same as the TLS client's: SNI + hostname checking + system CA, with no switch to turn it off).

Handshake and Frame Rules

  • The Upgrade request carries a random Sec-WebSocket-Key, and validates the Sec-WebSocket-Accept returned by the server;
  • Frames sent by the client are forcibly masked (RFC 6455 §5.3);
  • Fragmented messages are automatically reassembled by recv(); pings are automatically answered with pongs, and unsolicited pongs are ignored;
  • A peer close appears as an empty-payload message with opcode 8, after which calling close() releases the handle.

Function Table (Quoted Verbatim from sa_std/ws_client.sai)

SignatureDescription
sa_std_ws_client_supported(&out_supported: ptr) -> i32Whether the backend is available
sa_std_ws_client_connect(&url: ptr, url_len: u64, &out_handle: ptr) -> i32Build a connection from a ws:// / wss:// URL in one go (including Upgrade)
sa_std_ws_client_add_ca_file(&path: ptr, path_len: u64) -> i32Append a CA for wss:// (the first-wins rule is the same as the TLS client's)
sa_std_ws_client_send_text(handle: u64, &buf: ptr, len: u64) -> i32 / _send_binary(...)Send a single-frame text / binary message
sa_std_ws_client_ping(handle: u64, &buf: ptr, len: u64) -> i32Actively ping
sa_std_ws_client_recv(handle: u64, &out_opcode: ptr, &out_buf_handle: ptr) -> i32Receive one complete message; opcode: 1=text, 2=binary, 8=close
sa_std_ws_client_close(handle: u64, code: u16, &reason: ptr, reason_len: u64) -> i32Perform the close handshake and consume the handle
sa_std_ws_client_status_json(&out_handle: ptr) -> i32Capability/status JSON
sa_std_ws_client_buffer_data(buffer: u64) -> &ptr / _buffer_len(buffer: u64) -> u64 / _buffer_free(^buffer: u64) -> i32The message-payload buffer trio

Protocol Violation Detection

The following server violations cause recv() to return -5 (I/O error):

  • A frame from the server carries a mask (§5.1);
  • RSV1/2/3 are non-zero (no extension negotiated, §5.2);
  • A control frame is not FIN or its payload exceeds 125 bytes (§5.5); a close frame's payload is exactly 1 byte;
  • A text message's payload is not valid UTF-8 (§5.6).

Error Codes

The same as the TLS client: 0=OK, -1=unsupported, -5=I/O (including protocol violations), -12=OOM, -22=invalid argument, -100=TLS certificate verification failure for wss://.

NoteIPv6 works out of the box: the layer underneath uses tcpConnectToHost, and the [::1]:port form in a URL has been measured working over loopback.

Sources: ~/projects/sci/sa_std/ws_client.sai, src/runtime/sa_ws_client.zig (2026-09-19, verified: IPv4/IPv6 loopback echo, ping/pong, close, wss with a self-signed certificate + CA pinning, unpinned wss returning -100, and 4 kinds of protocol violations).
